title: What pushes a car forward?
hook: Press the pedal and the car pulls away. Something has to push it. What?

doesNotKnow: that a car's forward force comes from the road gripping the tyres
that the engine only turns the wheels, and internal forces cannot move the car

misconception: The engine pushes the car forward; friction only ever slows things down.
objective: The learner can explain that the engine only turns the wheels, the tyres push back on the road, and the road's grip pushing forward on the tyres is the force that speeds the car up, so with no grip the car cannot move however hard the wheels spin.

claims.text: Forces inside the car (engine on wheels, wheels on axles) come in equal and opposite pairs and cannot change the car's motion; only a force from outside can, so on a frictionless road the engine spins the wheels and the car stays put (stage: wheels turn, 0 N, car does not move; reveal: 'On a frictionless road the engine spun the wheels just as hard and the car went nowhere').
claims.source: Halliday, Resnick and Walker, Fundamentals of Physics, chapters on Newton's laws and on systems of particles (only external forces change the centre of mass's motion). Brief claim 1. | OpenStax University Physics (CC BY 4.0), github.com/openstax/osbooks-university-physics-bundle at 2300d5b: vol 1 m58323 'Center of Mass'; vol 1 m58295 'Forces' (added from FC pass 55, cm-physics R5).
claims.note: FC pass 55 (fact-checker, 2026-10-16): Opened OpenStax University Physics (CC BY 4.0), CNXML opened from github.com/openstax/osbooks-university-physics-bundle at 2300d5b (2026-09-08), vol 1 m58323 'Center of Mass': 'the total change of momentum of the entire object ... is due only to the external forces; the internal forces do not change the momentum of the object as a whole'; m58295 'Forces': 'only external forces acting on the free body affect its motion'. Stage seen: frictionless 0 N, 0 m/s2, wheels spin, no ghost outline (car did not move); reveal matches. The Halliday citation was not opened.

claims.text: The forward force on a driven car is static friction from the road on the tyres; the tyres push back on the road with an equal and opposite force (stage arrows 'road on tyre' forward and 'tyre on road' backward; reveal: 'The engine turns the wheels and the tyres push back on the road; the road pushing forward on the tyres is what moves the car').
claims.source: Halliday, Resnick and Walker, friction chapter and rolling without slipping (the friction on a driven wheel points forward). Newton's third law for the pair. Brief claim 2. | OpenStax University Physics (CC BY 4.0), github.com/openstax/osbooks-university-physics-bundle at 2300d5b: vol 1 m58299 "Newton's Third Law"; vol 1 m58719 'Work' (added from FC pass 55, cm-physics R5).
claims.note: FC pass 55 (fact-checker, 2026-10-16): Opened OpenStax University Physics (CC BY 4.0), CNXML opened from github.com/openstax/osbooks-university-physics-bundle at 2300d5b (2026-09-08), vol 1 m58299 'Newton's Third Law': 'A car accelerates forward because the ground pushes forward on the drive wheels, in reaction to the drive wheels pushing backward on the ground' and 'car tires push backward on road, reaction: road pushes forward on tires'; m58719 'Work': 'static friction of the road on the drive wheels'. Stage arrows 'road on tyre ->' and '<- tyre on road' seen (screenshots 02-03); reveal matches.

claims.text: A 1,200 kg car asking for 2.0 m/s² needs 2,400 N from the road (F = m a); a dry road (μ 0.8) can give up to 9,418 N, so the grip holds (stage readout '2,400 N forward · 2.0 m/s²'; Seen row 'dry: 2,400 N'; reveal 'your car gained speed at 2.0 m/s², pushed by the road's 2,400 N grip on the tyres').
claims.source: 1,200 × 2 = 2,400 N; 0.8 × 1,200 × 9.81 = 9,417.6 N. artifacts/scratch/cm-physics-r4/check.mjs (main checkout), block '63 what-pushes-the-car'. Demo.tsx M, A_ASK, MU. The μ values are illustrative (typical textbook ranges). recall.question: Why can't a car pull away on perfectly smooth ice, however powerful its engine?
options: The engine cannot turn the wheels on ice
Nothing outside pushes it forward: the road's grip on the tyres is the push
The ice pushes the car backwards harder than the engine pushes forwards
recall.why: The engine only turns the wheels. The forward push on the car comes from the road gripping the tyres, and smooth ice gives no grip, so the wheels just spin.
